$comment: Machine mirror of docs/toolchain/ontology.md. The `generated` gate renders that document's tables from this file, so the two cannot drift. Adding a kind or an invariant means editing this file and running `npm run gates:fix`.

adr.summary: This construct implements or depends on a decision record; an anchor names the clause.

item.summary: This construct is the work tracked by a work item.

invariant.summary: This construct establishes or relies on a named invariant from the table below.

doc.summary: Reference to a documentation section (the weakest binding; prefer a specific kind).

builder.immutable.meaning: No operation on a FenceBuilder mutates the receiver, its registry, its steps or any prototype; every operation returns a new builder.

registry.reserved-names.meaning: A validator may not be registered under a builder member name, an Object.prototype member name, `then`, `prototype` or `__proto__`; the check runs at compile time and at run time.

validator.plain-call.meaning: A validator is called as a plain function (`this` is undefined) with the subject followed by the recorded step arguments; exceptions it throws propagate unchanged.

memo.per-fence.meaning: A memoization cache belongs to one built Fence, keys primitives by SameValueZero and objects by identity, and caches every outcome including false.

result.vacuous-empty.meaning: An empty nested outcome collection counts as passed for `passed` and as not passed for `anyPassed`; explain() names it.

serialize.json-only.meaning: Only JSON values and fences may appear in step arguments; a fence nested in an argument is tagged `{"$fence": …}`; anything else is refused when serializing (strict) or described as a string (lenient, diagnostics only).

hydrate.validate-everything.meaning: fromJSON validates the whole document, including nested fences and every argument, and reports every unregistered validator name at once before building anything.
